quote: 1. Investing in stocks is an art, not a science, and people who've been trained to rigidly quantify everything have a big disadvantage.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 2. You can lose money in a very short time, but it takes a long time to make money.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 3. In my business a four bagger is nice, but a ten bagger is the fiscal equivalent of two home runs and a double.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 4. Frequently, there is no correlation between the success of a company's operations and the success of its stock over a few months or even years, but eventually, the correlation is 100 percent.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 5. Buy your straw hats in winter.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 6. The wonderful thing about the free market system is that eventually, brilliant ideas do get funded, and dumb ideas usually don't.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 7. Stop listening to professionals! Twenty years in this business convinces me that any normal person using the customary three percent of the brain can pick stocks just as well, if not better, than the average Wall Street expert.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 8. I'm always on the lookout for great companies in lousy industries.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 9. Find a company that no analyst has ever visited, or that no analyst would admit to knowing about, and you've got a double winner.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 10. The trick is not to learn to trust your gut feelings, but rather to discipline yourself to ignore them. Stand by your stocks as long as the fundamental story of the company hasn't changed.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 11. An important key to investing is to remember that stocks are not lottery tickets.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 12. In 99 cases out of 100, a house will be a money-maker.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 13. If you're lucky enough to have one golden egg in your portfolio, it may not matter if you have a couple of rotten ones in there with it.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 14. Although it's easy to forget sometimes, a share is not a lottery ticket. It's part ownership of a business.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 15. Everyone has the brainpower to follow the stock market. If you made it through fifth-grade math, you can do it.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 16. People worry about the riskiness of stocks, but bonds can be just as risky.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 17. Ultimately it is not the stock market nor even the companies themselves that determine an investor's fate. It is the investor.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 18. Investing is fun and exciting, but dangerous if you don't do any work.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 19. The key organ here isn't the brain, it's the stomach.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 20. In business, competition is never as healthy as total domination.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 21. If you can follow only one bit of data, follow the earnings — assuming the company in question has earnings. I subscribe to the crusty notion that sooner or later earnings make or break an investment in equities. What the stock price does today, tomorrow, or next week is only a distraction.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 22. Your investor's edge is not something you get from Wall Street experts. It's something you already have. You can outperform the experts if you use your edge by investing in companies or industries you already understand.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 23. Remember, things are never clear until it's too late.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 24. While catching up on the news is merely depressing to the citizen who has no stocks, it is a dangerous habit for the investor.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 25. The more cash that builds up in the treasury, the greater the pressure to piss it away.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 26. If you can't find any companies that you think are attractive, put your money in the bank until you discover some.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 27. I can't imagine anything that's useful to know that the amateur investor can't find out.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 28. Hidden-treasure companies: these are companies that have an asset you happen to know about but which professional investors have overlooked.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 29. It takes remarkable patience to hold on to a stock in a company that excites you, but which everybody else seems to ignore.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 30. Invest in simple companies that appear dull, mundane, out of favor, and haven't caught the fancy of Wall Street.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 31. Every stockholder should give as much time and attention to owning stocks as he or she would to choosing a refrigerator.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 32. Six months of a bear market is nothing more than a good excuse to buy your favorite stocks at bargain prices.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 33. Underneath, thousands of investors and speculators are trying to divine the market's message, and few of them agree from moment to moment.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 34. A successful stockpicker has the same relationship with a drop in the market as a Minnesotan has with freezing weather. You know it's coming, and you're ready to ride it out, and when your favorite stocks go down with the rest, you jump at the chance to buy more.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 35. Liking a store, a product, or a restaurant is a good reason to get interested in a company and put it on your research list, but it's not enough of a reason to own the stock.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 36. You get recessions, you have stock market declines. If you don't understand that's going to happen, then you're not ready, you won't do well in the markets.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 37. Far more money has been lost by investors preparing for corrections, or trying to anticipate corrections, than has been lost in corrections themselves.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 38. People who succeed in the stock market also accept periodic losses, setbacks, and unexpected occurrences. Calamitous drops do not scare them out of the game.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 39. This is one of the keys to successful investing: focus on the companies, not on the stocks.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 40. Go for a business that any idiot can run – because sooner or later, any idiot probably is going to run it.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 41. A correction is a wonderful opportunity to buy your favorite companies at a bargain price.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 42. Markets go down, sometimes they go down a lot. If you are not ready for this, you shouldn't own stocks.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 43. Long shots almost never pay off.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 44. Never fall in love with a stock; always have an open mind.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 45. Related diversification is one of the biggest disasters that can happen in business.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 46. The best stock to buy may be the one you already own.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 47. Just because you buy a stock and it goes up does not mean you are right. Just because you buy a stock and it goes down does not mean you are wrong.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 48. If you don't study any companies you have the same chance of success buying stocks as you do in a poker game if you bet without looking at your cards.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 49. Know what you own, and know why you own it.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 50. You should not buy a stock because it's cheap but because you know a lot about it.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 51. Avoid long shots. I've bought about 30 long shots in my life. I've never broken even on one.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 52. In this business if you're good, you're right six times out of ten. You're never going to be right nine times out of ten.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 53. Everyone has the brainpower to make money in stocks. Not everyone has the stomach. If you are susceptible to selling everything in a panic, you ought to avoid stocks and mutual funds altogether.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 54. The worst thing you can do is invest in companies you know nothing about. Unfortunately, buying stocks on ignorance is still a popular American pastime.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 55. I deal in facts, not forecasting the future. That's crystal ball stuff.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 56. The stock market demands conviction as surely as it victimizes the unconvinced.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 57. Owning stocks is like having children — don't get involved with more than you can handle.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 58. Absent a lot of surprises, stocks are relatively predictable over 10 to 20 years. As to whether they're going to be higher or lower in 2 or 3 years, you might as well flip a coin to decide.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 59. The person that turns over the most rocks wins the game. And that's always been my philosophy.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 60. When even the analysts at the brokerage houses ignore a stock, the astute investor gets an opportunity to buy a bargain.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 61. All you need for a lifetime of successful investing is a few big winners, and the willingness not to interfere with them.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 62. Every once in a while, the market does something so stupid it takes your breath away.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 63. A cocktail party can be a useful stock market indicator.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 64. The p/e ratio of any company that's fairly priced will equal its growth rate.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 65. Buy what you know.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 66. Gentlemen who prefer bonds don't know what they're missing.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 67. You can't see the future through a rearview mirror.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 68. When you sell in desperation, you always sell cheap.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 69. There is always something to worry about. Avoid weekend thinking and ignoring the latest dire predictions of the newscasters. Sell a stock because the company's fundamentals deteriorate, not because the sky is falling.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 70. Never invest in any idea you can't illustrate with a crayon.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 71. You don't have to be a rocket scientist. Investing is not a game where the guy with the 160 IQ beats the guy with the 130 IQ.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 72. The stock market isn't a casino, but you can turn it into one if you play switch the pig.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 73. If you stay half-alert, you can pick the spectacular performers right from your place of business or out of the neighborhood shopping mall, and long before Wall Street discovers them.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 74. Behind every stock is a company. Find out what it's doing.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 75. Debt is saving in reverse. The more it builds up, the worse off you are.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 76. Nobody can predict interest rates, the future direction of the economy or the stock market. Dismiss all such forecasts and concentrate on what's actually happening to the companies in which you've invested.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 77. Average investors can become experts in their own field and can pick winning stocks as effectively as Wall Street professionals by doing just a little research.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 78. If you can't convince yourself "When I'm down 25 percent, I'm a buyer" and banish forever the fatal thought "When I'm down 25 percent, I'm a seller," then you'll never make a decent profit in stocks.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 79. If you like the store, chances are you'll love the stock.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 80. Corporations, like people, change their names for one of two reasons: either they've gotten married, or they've been involved in some fiasco that they hope the public will forget.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 81. You can beat the market by ignoring the herd.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 82. If you can't explain to an 11-year-old in two minutes or less why you own the stock, you shouldn't own it.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 83. In dieting and in stocks, it is the gut and not the head that determines the results.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 84. Insiders might sell their shares for any number of reasons, but they buy them for only one: they think the price will rise.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 85. There's no shame in losing money on a stock. Everybody does it. What is shameful is to hold onto a stock, or worse, to buy more of it, when the fundamentals are deteriorating.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 86. The best time to invest is when you have money. This is because history suggests it is not timing which matters, it is time.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 87. In stocks, as in romance, ease of divorce is not grounds for getting married.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 88. Time is on your side when you own shares of superior companies.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 89. Selling your winners and holding your losers is like cutting the flowers and watering the weeds.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 90. If you spend more than 13 minutes analyzing economic and market forecasts, you've wasted 10 minutes.
speaker: Peter Lynch
